Set up Flutter project structure for off.body:
## Context
Create the initial Flutter app foundation described in README.md and ARCHITECTURE.md.

## Acceptance criteria
- Flutter project is initialized for Android and iOS.
- The app can run without login, cloud services, analytics, or remote backend configuration.
- Basic folder structure reflects presentation, application, and data layers.
- README development instructions are updated if setup commands are added.

Define local SQLite schema and migration.body:
## Context
The app stores all health-related data locally. ARCHITECTURE.md defines records, urination details, defecation details, tags, and record tag associations.

## Acceptance criteria
- SQLite tables exist for records, urination_details, defecation_details, tags, and record_tags.
- Records require occurred_at and at least one event type at application validation level.
- Tags use normalized_name as a unique value.
- record_tags associates tags with record_id and type: urination or defecation.
- Foreign keys cascade appropriately when records or tags are deleted.

Implement record repository and data acc.body:
## Context
Record persistence should be isolated in the data layer.

## Acceptance criteria
- Records can be created, read, updated, and deleted locally.
- Detail rows are created only for selected event types.
- Updating event type keeps detail rows and tag associations consistent.
- Repository methods support loading records with descriptions and tags for history and editing.

Implement tag repository and normalized.body:
## Context
Tags are global and reused across records using lower(trim(name)) normalization.

## Acceptance criteria
- Tags can be created, listed, updated, and deleted.
- Lookup by normalized name is available.
- Tag usage counts can be queried for filters and tag management.
- Duplicate normalized names are rejected or resolved to the existing tag.

Build quick record create and edit scree.body:
## Context
The main input flow lets users create or edit a bathroom record quickly.

## Acceptance criteria
- User can set date and time manually.
- User can select urination, defecation, or both.
- Urination fields appear only when urination is selected.
- Defecation fields appear only when defecation is selected.
- Save creates a new record or updates the existing record.

Validate that at least one event type is.body:
## Context
A record is invalid unless it includes urination, defecation, or both.

## Acceptance criteria
- Save is blocked or shows a clear validation message when neither type is selected.
- Validation applies during both creation and editing.
- The invalid state does not create partial database rows.

Keep urination and defecation details in.body:
## Context
A record can contain both event types, but each type has its own description and tags.

## Acceptance criteria
- Urination description is stored separately from defecation description.
- Urination tags are stored separately from defecation tags.
- Editing one event detail does not overwrite the other.
- History and CSV export display the correct detail per type.

Automatically create tags from record fo.body:
## Context
When users type a new valid tag while creating or editing a record, the app should create it automatically.

## Acceptance criteria
- New typed tag names create tags when saved or confirmed.
- Existing tags are reused by normalized name.
- Newly created tags receive a default random hexadecimal color.
- Empty tag names are never created.

Prevent empty and duplicate tag names.body:
## Context
Tags must be unique by lower(trim(name)) and cannot be empty.

## Acceptance criteria
- Empty or whitespace-only names are rejected.
- Names differing only by case or surrounding spaces are treated as duplicates.
- Duplicate attempts show a useful user-facing response or reuse the existing tag where appropriate.
- The same tag cannot be duplicated within the same record and event type.

Add editable hexadecimal tag colors.body:
## Context
Each tag has a color stored on the tag entity, not copied into records.

## Acceptance criteria
- New tags receive a random color_hex value.
- Users can edit color_hex manually from tag management.
- Invalid hex values are rejected.
- Updated colors appear wherever the tag is displayed.

Build history list with record summaries.body:
## Context
Users need a chronological view of all records.

## Acceptance criteria
- History shows date and time for each record.
- History indicates whether each record includes urination, defecation, or both.
- Associated tags are visible with their colors.
- Description previews appear when available.
- The list remains usable with many records.

Add record editing from history.body:
## Context
Users should be able to open existing records from history and edit them.

## Acceptance criteria
- Tapping a history item opens the edit flow with existing values populated.
- Saving updates the existing record instead of creating a duplicate.
- Cancel/back returns to history without unintended changes.

Add single, multiple, and all-record del.body:
## Context
The requirements include deleting one record, multiple selected records, and all records.

## Acceptance criteria
- A single record can be deleted.
- History supports multi-select deletion.
- Settings or another suitable place supports deleting all records.
- Deletions remove associated details and record tag rows.

Require confirmation before every delete.body:
## Context
Every delete operation must ask for confirmation before removing local health data.

## Acceptance criteria
- Single record delete shows confirmation.
- Multi-record delete shows confirmation.
- Delete-all shows confirmation with clear wording.
- Canceling a confirmation leaves data untouched.

Build combined filters for date range, e.body:
## Context
Filters must be combinable across date range, event type, and tags.

## Acceptance criteria
- Date range filter can be applied.
- Event type filter supports selecting more than one type.
- Tag filter supports selecting multiple tags.
- Applying multiple filters narrows results together.
- Clearing filters restores the full history list.

Implement tag filter search, top tags, e.body:
## Context
The tag filter should behave like a retail brand filter.

## Acceptance criteria
- Search input appears below the tag filter title.
- Top 3 most used tags are shown first.
- Users can expand to show all tags.
- Usage count appears next to each tag name, for example: pain (4).
- Selecting multiple tags works together with other filters.

Build tag management screen.body:
## Context
Users need direct control over global tags.

## Acceptance criteria
- Screen lists all tags.
- User can create a tag.
- User can edit tag name.
- User can edit tag hexadecimal color.
- User can delete a tag after confirmation.
- Usage count is visible for each tag.

Propagate tag edits and deletions across.body:
## Context
Tags are global entities referenced by records.

## Acceptance criteria
- Editing a tag name updates all records that display that tag.
- Editing a tag color updates all records that display that tag.
- Deleting a tag removes its associations from all records after confirmation.
- Deleting a tag does not delete records.

Implement manual CSV export with one row.body:
## Context
CSV export should be local, manual, and use one row per physiological event.

## Acceptance criteria
- Export includes columns occurred_at,type,description,tags.
- A record with both urination and defecation exports two rows.
- Tags are separated with semicolons.
- Export does not require cloud storage.
- Export uses system file picker or share sheet where possible.

Add settings screen with privacy, export.body:
## Context
README.md lists the Settings screen contents.

## Acceptance criteria
- Settings includes CSV export.
- Settings includes delete all records.
- Settings includes privacy statement.
- Settings includes app version.
- Settings includes owner/developer information.
- Settings includes a contact option for feedback, bug reports, or feature requests.

Document offline privacy guarantees in t.body:
## Context
The app stores sensitive health-related data only on device.

## Acceptance criteria
- In-app privacy copy explains that data stays local.
- Copy states there is no login, cloud storage, analytics, ads SDK, Firebase, Google services, Meta services, or external tracking.
- Copy clarifies that PIN/biometric lock is not implemented in-app and users can rely on device security.

Implement Android launcher widget quick.body:
## Context
Android launcher widget support should be prioritized first.

## Acceptance criteria
- Widget offers + Urination, + Defecation, + Both, and Open full record.
- Quick actions create a record with the current date and time.
- Quick-created records have no description or tags by default.
- Widget does not display recent records.
- Created records are visible and editable in app history.

Decide whether iOS launcher widget belon.body:
## Context
iOS widget support may be added later if it increases MVP complexity.

## Acceptance criteria
- Product/technical tradeoff is documented.
- Decision states whether iOS widget support is MVP or post-MVP.
- Follow-up implementation issue is created or updated if iOS widget support is kept.

Avoid Google, Meta, Firebase, analytics,.body:
## Context
The core privacy promise is that the app is fully offline and avoids external tracking or cloud dependencies.

## Acceptance criteria
- Dependency choices are reviewed before adding SDKs.
- No Firebase, analytics, ads SDK, Google services, Meta services, cloud login, cloud storage, or external backend is configured.
- Any dependency that could perform network access is justified before use.

Minimize mobile permissions for storage.body:
## Context
CSV export should avoid broad storage permissions.

## Acceptance criteria
- Export implementation uses system picker/share sheet where possible.
- Android permissions are kept minimal.
- iOS permissions are kept minimal.
- Permission prompts, if any, are explained by the OS flow or app UI.

Add app version and owner/developer info.body:
## Context
Settings should expose basic app and owner/developer information.

## Acceptance criteria
- App version is visible in Settings.
- Owner/developer information is visible in Settings.
- Information is easy to update for releases.

Add feedback, bug report, or feature req.body:
## Context
Users should have a way to contact the owner/developer.

## Acceptance criteria
- Settings includes a contact option.
- Contact option can support feedback, bug reports, and feature requests.
- The implementation does not introduce analytics or tracking.

Document future import, statistics, and.body:
## Context
ARCHITECTURE.md lists possible future features outside the current MVP.

## Acceptance criteria
- Future considerations are documented separately from MVP requirements.
- Import from CSV, statistics/trends, tag categories, structured observations, advanced filtering, and iOS widget support are clearly marked as future unless promoted by decision.
- No current MVP issue accidentally depends on these future features.
